what_happened: The job to use the earliest landing record for a job's landing and rebuild end was rejected at the final verdict. One of 6 acceptance criteria was unmet. That criterion is to run `athena status --snapshot <records directory>` on the real records and check that the landing duration printed for jobs npqp, pg2d, yp1e, abbg and 4z98 is within 15 minutes of the outcome-to-main-push gap, which is expected to be 5 to 12 minutes and taken from main-branch commit times in git log. The verifier gave one major finding and no blockers: behavior criterion 4 is unmet because its evidence must cite commands that ran (D43). The event lists no failed checks.
cause: Nothing before the final verdict checks that a behavior criterion's required evidence, which is command runs on real records cited in the report, will exist. The criterion needs a run against the real records directory and git log. The producer is not told that D43 rejects evidence that does not cite commands that ran. Nothing makes the producer run the command and record its output. The same job family keeps failing this way on D43 evidence.
other_causes: The criterion depends on real records and git history that the isolated producer or verifier may not be able to reach, so the run may have been impossible there.
The criterion's tolerance wording (15 minutes, an expected 5 to 12, and up to 27 tolerance) is loose and hard to cite as a pass.
open_hypotheses: The producer may never have run the status command on the real records.
The producer may have run it but not cited the commands in a form the verifier accepts.
The measured durations may have been outside the tolerance, so the criterion would be unmet even with proper evidence.
contradictions: The verifier's one major finding cites missing command evidence (D43), not a wrong landing duration. This suggests the work may be correct and only the evidence is missing.
No checks failed, unlike the two earlier cases in this family, which also had a failed test check.
prevention: Add a default for the producer and reading. Any criterion that needs a command run on real data must be run during the job, and its report must quote the command and its output. Before the final verdict, Athena should record the run itself, or fail early if the data is unreachable. The same default should say that evidence cited for D43 means commands that ran.
proposed_request: Re-run job 20261107-231406-f1bx. Use the earliest landing record for a job's landing and rebuild end in `athena status`. Run `cargo run -p athena-cli -- status --snapshot <records directory>` on the real records. For jobs npqp, pg2d, yp1e, abbg and 4z98, compare the landing duration printed with the gap between the outcome and the main-branch push taken from git log commit times. Each must be within 15 minutes of that gap, and the expected range is 5 to 12 minutes. Cite the exact commands you ran and their output in the report so the evidence meets D43. If the real records or git log cannot be reached, say so and stop instead of guessing. Also run cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings and cargo test, and add the CHANGELOG.md entry.
